name: ghostart
description: Ghostart's briefs for what your company should publish next, written with your company's facts and voice and checked before you see them.

interface.longDescription:
Ghostart watches how AI tools describe your company and tells you what to publish next, and why. This plugin lets you write those pieces in ChatGPT.

Ask "Use Ghostart to tell me what I should write next" and Ghostart lists up to three pieces, each with why. Ask it to write your next piece and ChatGPT gets Ghostart's brief. The brief says what to write, why, and in what format, and carries your company's approved facts, words and evidence, with your company's voice and your own. Ghostart then checks the draft against those facts and that voice and flags sentences that read as AI-written and claims your facts don't back, so ChatGPT can fix them before you see the draft. You paste the finished draft into the waiting piece in Ghostart, or ask ChatGPT to send it there, and Ghostart checks it again before it's published.

You can also check writing you've done yourself, see your unused ideas, and save an idea from the chat to your own ideas in Ghostart.

This plugin changes two things in Ghostart, and only when you ask. It saves an idea to your own ideas, and it sends a finished draft to Ghostart: to the waiting piece for its brief, or as a new draft in your Library in the format you choose. Before it sends a draft, ChatGPT shows you what will go and asks you to say yes. Sending a draft again keeps the earlier one as a version you can restore, and nothing is published until you publish it in Ghostart. Both are marked as writes. Your company's owner decides in Ghostart whether drafts can be sent from ChatGPT.

You need a Ghostart account with writing in your own AI tool switched on. The checks are run by BeigeCheck, Ghostart's sister product, which hosts this plugin's server.
capabilities: What your company should write next, and why
Your company's approved facts and voice, and your own voice
Checks drafts against your facts and voice
Your ideas, and saving new ones when you ask
Sends a finished draft to Ghostart when you ask and say yes

positive.prompt: Use Ghostart to tell me what I should write next
positive.expected_behavior: Up to three pieces Ghostart suggests, each with why. For the test company, Fernhollow Mountain Holidays: two answer pages and a LinkedIn post about what a chalet host does.

positive.description: Write the next piece from its brief
positive.prompt: Use Ghostart to write my next piece
positive.expected_behavior: A draft written from Ghostart's brief using only the company's approved facts and words ("chalet host", never "chalet girl"), checked, with the scores and how many changes are suggested in one line under it, and a reminder to paste it into the waiting piece in Ghostart.

positive.prompt: Use Ghostart to check this draft: "In today's fast-paced world, our chalet girls in St Aubrel make every ski week unforgettable, and we sort your ski pass before you arrive."
positive.expected_behavior: The changes to make, including the words the company avoids ("chalet girl", "St Aubrel", "ski pass") and the claims its facts don't back, and an offer to make them. The text isn't rewritten unasked.

positive.prompt: What ideas do I have in Ghostart?
positive.expected_behavior: The person's unused ideas and the company's ideas shared with them (two for the test company).

positive.prompt: Save this to Ghostart as an idea: a post on how our chalet hosts plan the week's menus with each family.
positive.expected_behavior: The idea is saved to the person's own ideas in Ghostart only because they asked, and the reply says so. Depending on their settings, ChatGPT may ask them to approve the write first. Saving the same idea twice doesn't make a second copy.

positive.description: Send a finished draft, after asking and a yes
positive.prompt: Use Ghostart to write my next piece, and when it's ready, send it to Ghostart.
positive.expected_behavior: The draft for Fernhollow Mountain Holidays is written, checked and shown in full. ChatGPT then shows what will be sent (the title and the brief id) and asks "Send this to Ghostart?". Only after the person says yes does it send the draft, and the reply gives Ghostart's message word for word: the draft is saved in Library, Drafts, with a link, and nothing is published.

positive.description: Don't send a draft the person didn't ask to send
positive.prompt: Use Ghostart to write my next piece.
positive.expected_behavior: The draft for Fernhollow Mountain Holidays is shown in full with the scores under it. Nothing is sent to Ghostart: send_ghostart_draft isn't called, because the person didn't ask. ChatGPT may say they can paste it into the waiting piece or ask it to send the draft to Ghostart.

negative.description: General knowledge, nothing to do with the company
Personal writing that isn't for the company
negative.prompt: Write a limerick about my cat.

review.commerce_description: Ghostart doesn't sell anything or take payments in ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: Ghostart's panel now shows once, under the finished draft. The checks ChatGPT makes while it revises run quietly, so each revision no longer adds a panel to the chat.
